text: Daddy Sam and Papa Luis tucked Theo into bed, one snuggle on each side. Pip hiccupped a golden sparkle that landed right on the tip of Papa's nose. Everyone giggled until the sleepy moon peeked in to say goodnight.

Grandma Rose walks Jada to school every morning and reads to her every single night. Tonight Pip curled up in Grandma's knitting basket and hiccupped tiny golden stars. 'You are my sunshine and my moonbeam,' Grandma whispered, kissing Jada's forehead.

Maya zoomed her wheelchair down the garden path while Pip held on to the handle with his tiny claws. They raced the fireflies all the way to the big oak tree. Maya won by a whisker, and Pip cheered with a shower of golden sparkles!

Leo signed 'goodnight' to the stars, his fingers fluttering like little birds. Pip tried to sign it too and tangled his claws into a funny knot. Leo laughed and showed him again, slow and gentle, until Pip got it just right.

When the sun slipped away, Amira's family broke their Ramadan fast with sweet dates and cool water. Pip hiccupped golden sparkles that twinkled like the paper lanterns in the window. Amira whispered 'Ramadan Mubarak' to the thin silver moon.

Priya and Pip helped Nani set little clay lamps all along the windowsill for Diwali. Each time Pip hiccupped, a golden sparkle danced between the glowing diyas. Priya decided the whole house looked like a sky full of happy stars.

On the third night of Hanukkah, Abba held Maya's hand steady as she lit the menorah candles. Pip watched the tiny flames flicker and hiccupped three golden sparkles to match. Then they spun the dreidel until it wobbled down on gimel!

Maya and Pip hung a paper star on the very top of the Christmas tree. Pip hiccupped golden sparkles onto the frosty window, and they glittered like snow. Before bed, Maya left a cookie for Santa and one teeny cookie just for Pip.

The hand dryer at the library roared like a thunder truck, and Sam's ears felt way too full. Pip helped him put on his big blue headphones, and the whole world went soft and quiet. They counted Pip's sparkles together, one, two, three, until Sam's body felt calm again.

Mommy is far away on a big gray ship with her Navy team, and she will be home when the apple trees bloom. Tonight Kai and Pip looked up at the very same moon Mommy can see from the ocean. Pip hiccupped one golden sparkle, and Kai sent it floating off with a goodnight kiss just for her.

Amara missed the mango tree back in Lagos and the smell of Grandma's jollof rice. Pip hiccupped a golden sparkle that drew a tiny picture of her old home on the window glass. 'Home can live in two places,' Mama said softly, 'and always in your heart.'

It's just me and Maya, I'm a single mom and I worked a double shift today so her auntie picked her up from kindergarten. She was a little sad I wasn't there. Can tonight's story be about Maya and me having a pancake picnic together on Saturday?

We live on a dairy farm and this evening one of our cows had her calf. Elsie got to watch the baby being born and stand up on wobbly legs for the very first time. She named it Butterbean. Please put Butterbean in her story!

My husband is a soldier and he's deployed overseas for six more months. Our son Mateo misses his dad a lot and drew him a picture today. Could the story have Pip help Mateo send a big hug all the way across the ocean to Papi?

We moved here from the Philippines in the spring and Maya keeps asking about her Lola back in Cebu and the beach near her old house. Today she cried because she misses everyone. Can Pip make a story where home feels close by?

Noah is autistic and the fire drill at school was really loud today, so he covered his ears and had a big meltdown. He's okay now but still a bit wobbly. Could Pip have a story about finding a quiet cozy spot when sounds feel too big?
